body:
# Independent audit of codimension-two contact stress elimination

Audited source: `candidate 860152d497c5cff4`, with
the finite pair compatibility model and normalized cap-gradient
separation used there.

The mechanism is valid under its unrestricted polytopal local-minimum
hypothesis. It does not apply to a minimum known only in a fixed shared
plane-count class. This distinction is a substantive remaining issue,
not a technicality resolved by the truncation argument.

## 1. Uniform zero-cost truncation

Fix a full-dimensional d-polytope K, d≥2, and a nonzero exposing
normal n whose face F has dimension k≤d−2. A finite vertex
triangulation of K gives, on each simplex meeting F, a normal deficit
Σ δ_iλ_i over the vertices off F, with each δ_i>0. If the simplex
face in F has dimension f≤k, there are d−f off-face barycentric
coordinates. A removed point has each such coordinate at most a
constant times t. Integration in simplex coordinates bounds the
removed volume by O(t^(d−f)), hence O(t^(d−k))=O(t²).
Simplices with no vertex in F have a positive minimum deficit and
contribute nothing for small t.

For any measurable cap A, even one changing with t,

    ||K∩A|−|K(t)∩A||≤|K\K(t)|.

This is the required uniformity over all cap orientations, thresholds,
and boundary coincidences. It does not require differentiating the cap
normal. A nearby affine image changes the removed volume only by its
bounded determinant factor. For finitely many simultaneous cuts the
union bound gives O(Σ_l σ_l²)=O(||σ||²), uniformly over the nonnegative
orthant and nearby affine parameters. Thus all objective and cap
derivatives in the new cut coordinates are zero, including joint
directions involving old body and cap parameters.

## 2. The near-normal support estimate

The vertex argument in the source is sound. Near n, old maximizing
vertices belong to F, because all other old vertices have a fixed
positive n-deficit. New cut vertices lie on edges joining a vertex
v∈F to an old vertex outside F and have the form v+t a_e, where
n·a_e=−1 and the finite list of a_e is fixed.

Hence for m near n,

    m·(v+t a_e)≤h_K(m)−t(1−C|m−n|).

Old vertices outside F cannot maximize the cut body for sufficiently
small t: they retain a fixed support gap, whereas an edge leaving an
old maximizing vertex supplies a cut point only O(t) below h_K(m).
This proves the support-improvement estimate uniformly in the stated
neighborhood. It also proves h_{K(t)}(n)=h_K(n)−t.

After an affine endpoint map A_e x+c_e, the comparison normal is
A_e^T n_l(p), which differs from n_l by O(|p|). Thus the indexed cut
improves its support by σ_{e,l}+O(|p|σ_{e,l}). Other cuts can only
improve that support further. No assumption about which of the tied
old vertices becomes the maximizer is made.

## 3. Actual realization of the inner compatibility cone

For three fibers at 0,1,2, the middle facet inequalities and every pair
of endpoint vertices give a finite smooth system g_{l,ab}(p)≥0
before truncation. All originally active pairs are retained. The
actual support gap after truncation is bounded below by

    min_{a,b}g_{l,ab}(p)+Σ_eσ_{e,l}+O(|p|Σ_eσ_{e,l}).

Therefore a direction satisfying every active linearized pair
inequality strictly, with σ≥0, integrates along p=tδp, σ=tδσ to a
genuinely compatible family for all sufficiently small t>0.
Nonactive pairs retain their gaps. Cap-cover constraints are linear
and remain exact; they need no second-order approximation.

There is an appropriate strictification direction for this three-fiber
model. Choose interior q_0,q_2 and q_1=(q_0+q_2)/2. The latter is
interior to K_1 because the endpoint Minkowski midpoint contains a
ball about it. A common homothetic shrink about these three compatible
points preserves every active midpoint equality. Its inward velocity
is strictly negative on every body facet, so it strictly decreases
every admissible active-cap gradient: each cap has a positive boundary
patch in its open side. Add a sufficiently small middle-only outward
homothety about q_1. On each active middle facet its compatibility
derivative is positive, while all cap-gradient decreases remain strict.

This direction has σ=0, which is permitted. It need not make the
σ≥0 constraints strict: those constraints are linear and an eventual
candidate direction with σ≥0 already satisfies them exactly.
It does make every nonlinear compatibility constraint's first-order
margin strict. Adding a sufficiently small multiple to a separated
improving direction preserves its positive objective derivative and
produces actual feasible competitors.

Thus the separation proof is supported by a realizable inner cone;
the source does not silently identify a formal tangent cone with the
true nonlinear feasible set.

## 4. Closed cone, normalization, and multiplier sign

The active cap-gradient sets in the enlarged parameter space have
zero σ-coordinates and are compact and convex. The strictification
direction belongs to the sufficient feasibility cone and pairs
strictly negatively with every one of these cap gradients. The usual
argument therefore closes their convex conic hull plus the polar of
the polyhedral feasibility cone: pairing with this direction bounds
the total nonnegative cap coefficient in any convergent sequence.

Normalized separation then gives

    objective gradient
      =Σ_j λ_j cap-gradient_j
       −Σ_{l,ab}η_{l,ab} Dg_{l,ab}
       −Σ_{e,l}ζ_{e,l} Dσ_{e,l}
       + the cap-cover/equality terms,

where all λ,η,ζ are nonnegative. The objective is normalized to one;
it is not an abnormal multiplier assertion. Joint continuous
homothety still supplies the ordinary exact normalization because
the active compatibility gaps are zero and σ remains zero.

In coordinate σ_{e,l}, the objective and every cap derivative are
zero. The pair compatibility coefficients are +1, while the
nonnegative-coordinate constraint has coefficient +1. Thus

    0=−Σ_{a,b}η_{l,ab}−ζ_{e,l}.

The sign is correct, and nonnegativity forces the aggregate contact
multiplier to vanish. Ties among endpoint support vertices do not
weaken this conclusion. Adding several cuts at once introduces no
negative σ coefficient that could cancel it.

## 5. Exact geometric and variational scope

At an unrestricted positive polytopal local minimum, the argument
therefore produces a normalized stress supported only on middle-facet
normals exposing facets in both endpoints. It does not remove the
geometric contact itself, and it need not make every preexisting
stress have this property.

The guaranteed attained polytopal minimum in a fixed shared-N class
is insufficient: corner truncations can require additional shared
planes. The unrestricted attained minimum from the canonical-lift
reduction is not currently known to be polytopal. Consequently the
two existence statements cannot be combined to drop this hypothesis.

For the planar triangle consequence, once all contact multipliers
vanish the central affine equations again imply bisected sections and
the weighted triangle bound. At a merely active containment, the
claim that at most one endpoint is deepest must use the separately
proved midpoint depth-plus-min estimate; strict Brunn–Minkowski alone
no longer gives it. The elementary centroid version already suffices
for triangles with equally deep endpoints.

## 6. General finite bases: extreme sources only

For a projection-extreme index e, no nontrivial anchored convex
representation has target e. Truncating its fiber therefore cannot
worsen an incoming target condition. In each support constraint

    h_{K_z}(n)≥Σ_w p_w h_{K_w}(n),

a cut of K_e in the indexed direction supplies the nonnegative bonus
p_eσ. Other source constraints may ignore their further improvements.
If a normalized separation can be rerun in the enlarged cut-parameter
family, the σ equation is a sum of nonpositive terms and eliminates
every positively weighted indexed nonfacet contact.

Projection extremality alone does not establish a strictification
condition for all other coupled targets in an arbitrary finite base.
The general statement remains conditional on a realizable normalized
variational representation for the enlarged family, not merely on
the existence of an old stress before the new variables are added.
For a nonextreme source, incoming target constraints can contribute
with the opposite sign, so no elimination follows from this argument.
